issues.title: 24 – 30 August 2026
issues.summary: The tariff, explained — an old quarrel reopened at full volume. The Long Read takes the machine apart: what a tariff is, who actually pays (buyers, near enough all of it), and the arc from Smoot-Hawley to the WTO, pegged to a week when Trump's US-Canada talks collapsed and a new China tariff loomed. Around it: Norway gets a king as Haakon VIII succeeds Harald V; Norris wins a dramatic Dutch GP as Verstappen crashes out on lap one and Antonelli's title lead swells to fifty-nine; Serie A opens with Juventus grinding out a 1-0; Elden Ring reaches Switch 2 and GTA VI gets its Netflix Extended Look.

issues.title: 17 – 23 August 2026
issues.summary: The Impossible Job — how the Premier League and EFL fixture list is actually built, anchoring the week the domestic season reopened: Arsenal took the Community Shield, the Premier League and Serie A kicked off, and a promoted Hull City beat Manchester United 2-0. Norris took pole for the Dutch Grand Prix as F1's title race resumed with Antonelli fifty clear.

issues.title: 10 – 16 August 2026
issues.summary: The Readiness Verdict — the wrist goes medical-grade with Google's Pixel Watch 5, and the Long Read asks whether a watch can actually call your recovery. Around it the domestic season nears its restart, F1's title race sits frozen with Antonelli fifty clear, and Hormuz is demoted after two more tanker strikes.

issues.title: 3 – 9 August 2026
issues.summary: The Strait and the Toll — a tanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz meets four official descriptions of one chokepoint in a single week, as Europe bakes to record heat, the Burnham government firms its cost-of-living package, and the Perseids peak under a new moon.

issues.title: 27 July – 2 August 2026
issues.summary: The Commonwealth Games close in Glasgow — Australia runs away with it, Scotland takes a record thirteen golds — and the Long Read tells how the Games nearly died and how Glasgow rescued them by shrinking. Norris wins in Hungary before F1's August break, the Bank of England holds a fifth time, and Halo reaches PlayStation.

issues.title: 20–26 July 2026
issues.summary: The first ordinary week under a PM nobody elected — Burnham finishes his cabinet, cuts an electricity-bill tax and caps bus fares. Halo reaches PlayStation 25 years late, F1 heads to Budapest, and a corroded lump of Greek bronze turns out to be a 2,000-year-old computer.

issues.title: The 2026 World Cup
issues.summary: Spain finish it unbeaten in New Jersey, Messi leaves in tears, and the first 48-team World Cup ends with the best third-place game ever played. Thirty-nine days, 104 matches, 308 goals — the whole tournament, filed.

issues.title: 13–19 July 2026
issues.summary: Seven leaders in a decade, and the newest reaches No.10 without an election — Andy Burnham, declared Labour leader unopposed, is sworn in as Prime Minister this week. A Sunday of unresolved handovers: the World Cup final and the Belgian Grand Prix are both still to play as the coffee cools, Sinner defends Wimbledon, Mariner 4's first look at Mars turns sixty-one, and the mortgage price war deepens before the Bank's next call.

issues.title: 7–13 July 2026
issues.summary: The night the world went live — sixty-four years on from Telstar's first live transatlantic broadcast, the week runs on signals across distance: Sinner defends Wimbledon, the World Cup pares to a heavyweight last four, the Gulf ceasefire is declared over, Palworld leaves early access, and, home from Efteling, Block 3 of the training year begins.

issues.title: H1 2026 in Review
issues.summary: The first half of 2026 read as one story — a changing of the guard, from Arsenal ending a 22-year wait to a nineteen-year-old leading the F1 title race and Zverev breaking the Sinner–Alcaraz grip. The highs, the lows, what we missed, and the calls that will still matter in December.

issues.title: 29 June – 5 July 2026
issues.summary: America marks 250 years in a year that won't sit still, DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes one of the worst on record, the World Cup reaches the last 16 as Wimbledon's seeds tumble, Silverstone sets its grid, Silo widens its mystery, the Somme at 110, and why Zone 2 is personal.

issues.title: The Byzantine Empire
issues.summary: Eleven hundred years of Rome, in Greek, behind the great walls — from Constantine's New Rome in 330 to the fall in 1453, and how Byzantium's law, alphabet, faith and learning still shape the modern world.

issues.title: 22–28 June 2026
issues.summary: The week the ceasefires turned into paperwork — an Israel–Lebanon framework and a US–Iran nuclear roadmap with the ground still shooting; the 48-team World Cup hits the knockouts; The Bear bows out; Switch 2's port summer; and the science of a week off.

issues.title: 15–21 June 2026
issues.summary: Andy Burnham walks back into the Commons; the US–Iran ceasefire signed as Israel and Hezbollah trade fire; Antonelli takes a fourth straight Grand Prix; House of the Dragon returns at 97%; the Bank holds; and the caffeine question answered.

issues.title: Sixteen Sleeps to the Trip
issues.summary: A two-week build-up to the return to Efteling and Beekse Bergen: the rides worth the queue and a new-for-2026 drop tower, two nights in the Wonder Hotel's floating castle, the savannah you can watch from the lodge, the safari on foot and by boat, and the conservation work behind the fence — all car-free, all onsite.

issues.title: 1–7 June 2026
issues.summary: A US-mediated Israel–Lebanon ceasefire dies within a day as Hezbollah rejects disarmament under fire; Monaco and the Roland-Garros men's final fall on Sunday afternoon after Andreeva's record-young title and Antonelli's maiden pole; Summer Game Fest dates the Final Fantasy VII trilogy's finale; and The Session lands the leucine-threshold case for spreading protein across the day.

issues.title: 26 May – 1 June 2026
issues.summary: A rare vaccine-less Ebola races through DR Congo and Uganda as Iran walks out of talks and oil jumps ~8%; Roland-Garros blows open when a 19-year-old beats Djokovic and the Monaco GP looms; Mina the Hollower lands a 92; The Mandalorian & Grogu recalibrates Lucasfilm's budget maths; and the biggest study yet maps how many sets actually build muscle.

issues.title: How Rome Got an Emperor
issues.summary: From Augustus's Principate to open hereditary autocracy: how a civil-war victor turned naked power into a permanent office, how an un-inheritable job became a dynasty, and how it all burned out with Nero.
